note: Family 3 of 6 — SAME_CATEGORY_PARTIAL_OVERLAP::PARTIAL_OVERLAP_LIVE. 19 conflict rows over 16 sentences (three sentences produce more than one pair because they carry three overlapping records). Every sentence read against its drop.
whatThisFamilyTurnedOutToBe: One defect, fifteen times. The sentence splitter ends a sentence at a full stop it should not — a middle initial (Richard A., George W., Mark A., Howard L., Jack W., Parker J., Joseph R., John W., Michael S., Ashton B.), a title (Dr., Adm., Sen.) or U.S. So one sentence was certified TWICE: a HEAD that runs from the sentence start and stops short of the final character, and a TAIL that begins after the abbreviation. Neither is the sentence, and the two overlap across the middle. The repair widens the head to the whole sentence and withdraws the tail — which is why fifteen of these are B rather than E: nothing is being removed from the archive, one correct record is replacing two wrong ones.
theSixteenthIsDifferent: #4310 p4310-s015 is the sentence the owner already ruled on. A-SB-4310 withdrew its truncated Q-authored claim and recorded the sentence as SOURCE-OWNED — pasted Washington Post copy, `qAuthored: false`. Widening a claim back across it would undo that ruling, so the three fragments the ruling left behind are withdrawn instead, which is what A-SB-4310 says in its own words: 'the partial Q-authored span is withdrawn; the complete sentence is retained as source-owned'. Flagged for the owner because it extends a ruling of theirs.
